claim_verdicts.slide: ANN Index Families — HNSW, IVF-PQ, DiskANN
claim_verdicts.bullet: **HNSW** — navigable small-world graph kept in memory; tuned via M (connectivity), efConstruction (build quality), and efSearch (query exploration depth) [claim:agentic-de:037]
claim_verdicts.source_excerpt: A higher efSearch (e.g., 500 vs. 100) increases recall by exploring more neighbors, but it slows down queries due to additional distance calculations. In a 10-million-vector dataset, efSearch=500 might achieve 98% recall but take 5ms per query, while efSearch=100 might drop to 85% recall with 1ms latency. efSearch and efConstruction have no effect on the memory usage. A higher M (e.g., 24 vs. 12) increases the graph's connectivity, improving recall by reducing the chance of search getting trapped in local minima. However, more connections also expand the index size (memory usage) and slow down build time.

claim_verdicts.slide: Metadata Filtering, Consistency, and Silent Recall Loss
claim_verdicts.bullet: Metadata filtering interacts destructively with ANN graph traversal [claim:agentic-de:040]
claim_verdicts.source_excerpt: Naive pre-filtering achieves much lower recall than post-filtering, with maximum recall plateauing at ~57% compared to >99% for post-filtering. Non-matching nodes are not only poor result candidates, but also routing states that connect the search to other regions of the graph. Skipping their expansion prevents the search from reaching their neighbors, even when those neighbors match the predicate.
